text:
Of the two options in the note, the answer is D, prior to neck surgery. A tracheostomy is sometimes done beforehand to secure the airway before major head and neck surgery. It doesn't repair paralysed vocal cords, so A is out. I still think C (aiding ventilator weaning) is also a recognised indication, so my earlier answer wasn't unreasonable, but the note rules it out.

CONFIDENCE: 70
